purpose: Measure whether training on the isolated R1.5 front-to-back coverage-splat candidate improves localization on the already-used common Direct-HDR development reference; not a ranking or held-out test.

candidate_event_source.radiance_units: scene-linear renderer radiance; not display grayscale or calibrated W/m^2/sr
candidate_event_source.geometry_inputs: cached depth, segmentation, camera pose and object poses used inside event generation only
candidate_event_source.coverage_resolve: front-to-back bilinear-footprint coverage with 1e-5 m depth tie band; incomplete support normalized over observed support
candidate_event_source.endpoint_composite: same diagnostic next-primary convention: prefer endpoint 1 where supported, then endpoint 0; midpoint hold for unsupported pixels; exact observed endpoint identity
candidate_event_source.sample_schedule: same frozen PhysicsInterpolator adaptive sampler and per-episode timestamps as the existing native-HDR generator; sampler inputs are evaluated without emitting legacy warped frames
candidate_event_source.temporal_radiance_limit: endpoint-only radiance and current hold rule remain; this experiment does not claim to repair unknown intermediate illumination or moving-shadow brightness

v2e_control.training_event_source: reuse the exact existing paired small9 V2E event source for provenance and split verification
v2e_control.model_checkpoint: reuse the fixed V2E checkpoint from the paired small9 development run

v2e_input_endpoint.source: reuse exact official V2E + SuperSloMo event archives from the paired small9 development batch

training.checkpoint_selection: same validation loss and early-stopping rule as the previous native-HDR development retrain

evaluation.reference: same nine-episode 2 kHz Direct-HDR event files and exact same pre-contact poll timestamps used by the previous R1 development comparison
models: previous native-HDR Ours checkpoint, rerun for a same-code control
evaluation.status: development only; the episodes have been inspected previously and are not a held-out test
